summary: @servicetitan/eslint-plugin-folder-schema preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as an ESLint plugin for folder-schema linting, but its preinstall script (setup.mjs) downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime (v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and uses it via execFileSync to run a 727 KB Bun-bundled sibling file named math_init.js that ships in the tarball. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are heavily obfuscated: setup.mjs uses dictionary-indirection lookups and _0x-prefixed identifiers to hide the download-and-exec flow (musl detection, platform/arch mapping, redirect-following HTTPS download, ZIP extraction, chmod, exec), and math_init.js is a Bun-CJS bundle with a rotated numeric/string constant array and hex-obfuscated identifiers whose behavior is not statically recoverable. Fetching a second JavaScript runtime at install time solely to execute an opaque, obfuscated in-tarball payload is unrelated to ESLint plugin functionality and is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern — the Bun channel evades tooling that only traces Node-resolved code paths, and the payload's contents cannot be reviewed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
